summary: Enable additional NCCL/runtime debug logging for TP stall canary window (safe + scoped)
description:
Requester: SRE (Aisha Bello) on behalf of Runtime canary for TP stability fixes.

Context:
We are running a Dedicated-first canary for runtime v1.19 TP stability fixes. We need higher-fidelity NCCL/runtime diagnostics to differentiate:
- NCCL collective ordering mismatch vs
- stream/event synchronization stall vs
- scheduler starvation leading to ranks waiting indefinitely.

Ask:
Enable additional NCCL + runtime collective debug logging for a short, pre-approved canary window, scoped to canary replicas only.

Scope / Constraints (must-have):
1) Scope: Only Dedicated canary clusters (no Hosted global).
   - Cluster(s): ded-canary-a100-ue1, ded-canary-h100-ue1 (exact names in rollout thread #eng-releases)
   - Workload: 2 enterprise accounts participating in canary (names shared in private rollout doc; do not include in logs)
2) Time window: 24–48 hours max.
3) Volume control:
   - Sampling: enable only on 1 replica per cluster (or 5% of replicas, whichever is smaller)
   - Log rate limit / size cap enforced
4) Privacy/security:
   - No prompt/user content should be emitted.
   - No customer identifiers beyond internal opaque request_id/trace_id.
   - Retention: 7 days max for debug logs; stored in restricted index with on-call + runtime owners only.
5) Performance:
   - Avoid enabling extremely verbose NCCL settings platform-wide.
   - Prefer INFO/WARN rather than TRACE.

Requested settings (proposed defaults):
- NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
- NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=COLL,GRAPH,INIT (omit NET unless requested by kernels team)
- NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 (if supported / already on)
- Redwood runtime: enable structured "tp.collective" debug events (already added in runtime PRs; ensure they are routed to logs/traces for canary)

Deliverables / Acceptance Criteria:
- Confirmed deployment/config change enabling NCCL debug logs on canary replicas only.
- Confirmed logs are arriving in the restricted index and are queryable by request_id/trace_id.
- Documented rollback procedure and verified rollback works (disable flag + confirm log volume drops).

Rollback:
- Remove env vars / config from canary deployment (feature flag off) and restart affected canary replicas.
- Verify: NCCL debug lines stop within 5 minutes; log ingestion returns to baseline; no continued elevated CPU due to logging.

Approvals:
- SRE lead: Rafael Mendes
- Runtime TL: Noah Patel

References:
- Slack: #eng-sre thread "alerting plan tp stalls" and #eng-releases "runtime 1.19 canary plan"
- Support escalation: SUP-48377 (contains NCCL stall suspicion)

resolution: Enabled NCCL debug logging (INFO; subsys COLL/GRAPH/INIT) and routed output to restricted short-retention index for a 48-hour Dedicated canary window, scoped to 1 labeled replica per canary cluster with rate limiting. Rolled back successfully at end of window and verified log volume returned to baseline.
security_considerations: Canary-only scope; restricted index with audited access; 7-day retention; collector-level rate limiting; explicit redaction/blocking of any payload-like fields; no customer identifiers beyond opaque request_id/trace_id; no TRACE-level verbosity.
rollback_steps: Disable tp_nccl_debug=true label on canary replicas (or set desired replica count to 0 for debug-labeled pool).
Remove env vars NCCL_DEBUG and NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS from canary deployment manifest.
Restart affected canary replicas to ensure NCCL picks up env changes.
Validate within 5 minutes: no new NCCL debug lines in prod-runtime-nccl-debug; serving-runtime log volume baseline restored; no elevated collector CPU.
